concepts.name: Meaning of Supply
concepts.description: Supply refers to the quantity of a commodity that producers are willing and able to offer for sale at different prices during a given period. Supply depends on both willingness and the ability to produce and sell.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to define supply and distinguish it from stock and production.

concepts.name: Determinants of Supply
concepts.description: Supply is influenced by factors such as the price of the commodity, production costs, technology, prices of related goods, government policies, and producers' expectations.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to identify and explain the major determinants of supply.

concepts.name: Individual and Market Supply
concepts.description: Individual supply refers to the quantity supplied by a single producer, while market supply represents the total quantity supplied by all producers in the market.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to differentiate between individual supply and market supply.

concepts.name: Law of Supply
concepts.description: The law of supply states that, other things remaining constant, the quantity supplied of a commodity increases when its price increases and decreases when its price decreases.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to explain the law of supply with suitable examples.

concepts.name: Supply Schedule and Supply Curve
concepts.description: A supply schedule presents the relationship between price and quantity supplied in tabular form, while a supply curve illustrates the same relationship graphically.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to prepare and interpret a supply schedule and supply curve.

concepts.name: Assumptions of the Law of Supply
concepts.description: The law of supply assumes that production technology, input prices, government policies, producer expectations, and other influencing factors remain unchanged.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to state the assumptions underlying the law of supply.

concepts.name: Extension and Contraction of Supply
concepts.description: Changes in quantity supplied due solely to changes in the commodity's own price result in movement along the supply curve.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to distinguish between extension and contraction of supply.

concepts.name: Increase and Decrease in Supply
concepts.description: Changes in supply caused by non-price factors lead to a shift of the entire supply curve either to the right or to the left.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to explain increases and decreases in supply using supply curve shifts.

concepts.name: Supply Curve Movements
concepts.description: Students learn the difference between movements along the supply curve and shifts of the supply curve resulting from changes in production conditions.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to interpret movements and shifts in a supply curve.

concepts.name: Price Elasticity of Supply
concepts.description: Price elasticity of supply measures the responsiveness of quantity supplied to changes in the price of a commodity.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to explain the concept of price elasticity of supply.

concepts.name: Degrees of Elasticity
concepts.description: Supply may be perfectly elastic, perfectly inelastic, relatively elastic, relatively inelastic, or unitary elastic depending on producers' responsiveness to price changes.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to classify different degrees of elasticity of supply.

concepts.name: Factors Affecting Elasticity of Supply
concepts.description: Elasticity of supply depends on production time, availability of resources, storage facilities, production flexibility, and technological conditions.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to explain the factors affecting elasticity of supply.

concepts.name: Business Production Decisions
concepts.description: Producers use supply analysis to determine production levels, allocate resources, and respond to market price changes.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to explain how supply analysis supports production planning.

concepts.name: Market Equilibrium
concepts.description: The interaction of supply and demand determines the equilibrium price and quantity in a competitive market.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to explain the role of supply in determining market equilibrium.

concepts.name: Government Policies and Supply
concepts.description: Taxes, subsidies, regulations, and technological support influence producers' willingness and ability to supply goods and services.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to analyze the impact of government policies on supply.

concepts.name: Understanding Supply
concepts.description: This chapter introduces the meaning of supply, determinants, the law of supply, supply schedules and curves, changes in supply, elasticity of supply, and their practical applications in markets.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to analyze supply behavior, interpret supply curves, explain elasticity, and apply supply concepts to real-world economic situations.
